blocks.text: What is this?
In JavaScript, the this keyword refers to an object.
The this keyword refers to different objects depending on how it is used:

rows: Alone, this refers to the global object.
In a function, this refers to the global object.
In a function, in strict mode, this is undefined.
In an object method, this refers to the object.
In an event, this refers to the element that received the event.

In methods like call(), apply()
and bind(), this can refer to any object.

blocks.text: this is not a variable.
this is a keyword.
You cannot change the value of this.
This Precedence
Use the following precedence of order to determine which object this refers to:

rows: this is in a function being called using bind()
this is in a function being called using apply()
this is in a function being called using call()
this is in an object function (method)
this is in a function in the global scope
